UnitStatement: Deliverable DEL-17-09 is named 'Export adapter SDK and additional targets' under Package PKG-17 'Export Format Interoperability'.
DEL-17-09 is of type API_CONTRACT.
DEL-17-09 covers scope items SOW-030, SOW-074, and SOW-075.
DEL-17-09 addresses objectives OBJ-009, OBJ-017, and OBJ-018.
DEL-17-09 is a contract-level adapter extensibility target sequenced after DEL-17-01 source basis and DEL-17-02 common export contracts.
DEL-17-09's contract surface is an adapter SDK contract, adapter template, target registry contract, and validation checklist at planning/contract level only.
DEL-17-09's primary upstream contract is the DEL-17-02 export package, profile, stable ID map, manifest, and loss-report contract.
DEL-17-01 admitted source basis and TBD register gate target-specific behavior for DEL-17-09.
Adapters validate units, provenance, diagnostics, redistribution, and public/private data boundaries, and cannot bypass validation, sandboxing, envelopes, or report controls.
Plugins and adapters are denied by default until a later approved permission/runtime design authorizes bounded capability.
Additional targets remain candidate targets until they provide public, official, project-owned, or rights-cleared source basis and explicit loss/TBD records.
Implementation code is out of scope: this Phase A deliverable does not create code, schemas, package manifests, sample adapters, public endpoints, runtime loaders, or compatibility artifacts.
The public API promise is out of scope: public API transport, endpoint syntax, plugin runtime, permission taxonomy, and exact code-generation tooling remain TBD.
Concrete additional target support is TBD; targets may be evaluated only after source basis, target version basis, rights posture, loss categories, and validation obligations are recorded.
External tool execution is optional/user-owned when applicable; external execution metadata must not imply bundled executables, license independence, formal validation, or professional acceptance.
Public artifacts must not include protected standards text, proprietary examples, private project data, code-specific values, or target files without redistribution rights.
DEL-17-09 constructs a contract-level adapter SDK admission model, not an SDK implementation, composed of four planning objects.

The adapter SDK contract defines the obligations an export adapter must satisfy before participating in the PKG-17 export package/profile/manifest/loss-report workflow; concrete runtime/API surface is TBD.
The adapter template describes expected evidence and checklist sections for future target adapters without providing implementation code or examples from proprietary formats.

The target registry contract defines target admission states, required source basis, boundary notes, target version basis, validation evidence, and unresolved-TBD tracking; no target is admitted by this deliverable.
The validation checklist lists checks for source basis, units, provenance, stable IDs, manifests, loss reports, diagnostics, privacy, protected-content screening, and professional-boundary wording.

An expected target registry/profile record includes target_name, admission state, target version basis or TBD, source-basis IDs or TBD, rights/redistribution posture, boundary notes, unresolved-TBD list, validation evidence reference, and a no-support/no-claim statement; exact field names remain TBD.

An expected source-basis record includes source location, license or redistribution basis, admitted use, boundary notes, affected target behavior, review disposition, and a source-basis ID whose exact field name remains TBD.

An expected validation checklist record includes checklist item, validation category, expected evidence artifact, result status (pass, fail, TBD, or not applicable), reviewer note, and a source or run-record reference; exact record format remains TBD.

DEL-17-09 is the boundary guide for future export adapters and additional targets, keeping extension work possible without weakening PKG-17 source-basis, stable-ID, loss-report, protected-content, privacy, diagnostics, or professional-boundary controls.
DEL-17-09 guidance is contract-level only and is not an implementation guide, public API promise, compatibility statement, or target support announcement.
Start from DEL-17-02 package/profile/stable-ID/manifest/loss-report contracts before considering any adapter-specific behavior.
Admit target behavior only from public, official, project-owned, user-provided-with-rights, or otherwise rights-cleared sources.
Keep candidate targets in a non-support state until source basis, target version basis, redistribution posture, validation expectations, and unresolved TBDs are recorded.
Treat every export as potentially lossy; require manifest, ID-map, diagnostics, and loss-report evidence even when the target file is produced.

Keep adapter work behind the same no-bypass controls as first-party export code: schema validation, unit checks, provenance, diagnostics, private-data controls, protected-content screening, report boundaries, and professional-boundary wording.
Prefer explicit TBD, unsupported, omitted, approximated, or delegated classifications over broad compatibility or support language.
Additional targets should move through conservative admission states.
Admission state 'Candidate' means a target has been named for possible future review, but no support is claimed.
Admission state 'Source-basis pending' means public or rights-cleared source evidence has not yet been admitted and target behavior remains TBD.
Admission state 'Source-basis admitted' means source evidence has been recorded with boundary notes, but support still depends on a later sealed implementation/validation deliverable.
Admission state 'Contract-ready' means the target profile can reference source-basis IDs, required fields, loss categories, stable-ID behavior, and validation obligations.
Admission state 'Implementation-gated' means future code/test work may be dispatched under a separate sealed deliverable; DEL-17-09 does not perform that work.
Admission states must not be used as release, compatibility, vendor-certification, or professional acceptance states.

The SDK surface should be described as obligations and review checkpoints until a later implementation brief authorizes code; useful obligations include source basis, profile metadata, stable identity, package member declaration, loss reporting, diagnostics, protected-content screening, privacy classification, and professional-boundary wording.
Exact adapter method names, schemas, endpoints, loader mechanisms, and package structure remain TBD.

Adapter SDK contract denotes the normative obligation set for future exporters: source basis, target profile intake, validation, stable identity, loss reporting, diagnostics, privacy, protected-content screening, and professional-boundary controls.
SDK surface denotes the future runtime/API methods, schemas, loader mechanics, and package structure, which remain TBD until later sealed implementation work.

Target profile contract denotes the per-target declaration of target family, target version basis, source-basis IDs, unit and coordinate policy, supported/unsupported behavior, loss policy, and validation policy.

Target registry contract denotes the admission record for candidate/source-basis/contract-ready/implementation-gated target states, and is not a release, compatibility, or professional-acceptance registry.

Additional targets may include plant-design exchanges, solver-neutral packages, geometry exports, or user-owned APIs only when the target brings a source basis and rights posture; a target name alone is not evidence and common industry practice is not enough to close target behavior gaps.
If a future adapter involves a downstream executable or hosted service, that execution must remain optional and user-owned unless a later human authority explicitly approves a different boundary.
A successful external run may be recorded as regression or handoff evidence but must not be described as professional acceptance, formal validation, code compliance, or vendor certification.

External-run evidence is admissible only as bounded technical evidence when the user controls the executable/service, has the legal right to run it, preserves run artifacts, and records the target version, profile version, manifest or run record, and limitations.
Exclude or quarantine external-run evidence when licensing, redistribution, private-data, protected-content, provenance, or target-version basis is unclear.

Treat external-run evidence as non-authoritative context that supports regression or handoff review but does not close source-basis, code-compliance, professional-acceptance, or formal-validation questions.

Trade-off (community extensibility vs. governance control): favor a narrow admission contract with required evidence and loss reporting; a target can remain useful while still carrying explicit limitations.
Trade-off (broad target list vs. source quality): keep unsupported targets as candidates and admit fewer targets with stronger source basis instead of naming many targets as supported.
Trade-off (adapter convenience vs. stable identity): require stable ID maps and sidecars where target artifacts cannot carry canonical IDs directly.
Trade-off (fast file writing vs. auditability): validation, manifests, diagnostics, and loss reports are part of the export outcome, not optional extras.
Trade-off (target-specific options vs. local code-checking): pass-through target options may be recorded as target configuration but shall not become OpenPipeStress code-checking logic.

Acceptable contract-level example: a future target registry entry names a target as Candidate, records source-basis status as TBD, states that no support is claimed, and lists required evidence before implementation can be dispatched.

Acceptable public template example: an invented adapter checklist uses synthetic target names and invented model references to show where source basis, stable ID behavior, loss categories, and boundary notes would be recorded.
Not acceptable: a public fixture copied from a vendor sample, standards table, protected format manual, private project file, or licensed report without documented redistribution rights.

Not acceptable: a statement that a named target is compatible, supported, validated, code-compliant, accepted for professional use, or release-ready before source basis and later sealed validation work exist.

UnitStatement: The DEL-17-09 procedure defines how future work should use the adapter SDK and target-admission contract for source intake, target admission, adapter review, validation planning, and closeout.
The DEL-17-09 procedure does not implement adapters, schemas, code, tests, public API endpoints, runtime loaders, or target-specific writers.
Prerequisite: read the DEL-17-01 four-document kit, Source_Basis_Register.md, and CAEPIPE_Question_Dossier.md when the target is affected by PKG-17 source-basis rules.
Prerequisite: read the DEL-17-02 four-document kit and use its export package, profile, stable-ID, manifest, and loss-report contract objects.
Prerequisite: confirm the target has public, official, project-owned, user-provided-with-rights, or otherwise rights-cleared source evidence.
Prerequisite: confirm protected standards data, proprietary examples, private project data, copied vendor files, and license-bypass material are not being introduced.

Prerequisite: confirm runtime permission, sandbox, public API transport, package layout, concrete schema layout, external execution, and target-specific validation remain TBD unless a later sealed brief authorizes them.
To register a candidate target, record the target name only as a candidate.
When registering a candidate target, record source-basis status as TBD until source evidence is admitted.
When registering a candidate target, record that no support, compatibility, validation, release, code-compliance, or professional-acceptance claim is made.
When registering a candidate target, record any known IP, license, privacy, or redistribution concern as a blocker or TBD.
When registering a candidate target, record the target-admission decision artifact as TBD unless a later sealed brief names a registry file, run record, or decision log.

To admit source basis, classify each source as public official documentation, public specification, project-owned material, user-provided rights-cleared material, private-only material, or rejected/quarantined material.
When admitting source basis, reject or quarantine suspected protected standards content, proprietary examples, copied target files, private project data, or unclear-redistribution material.
When admitting source basis, record source location, license or redistribution basis, admitted use, boundary notes, and affected target behavior.
When admitting source basis, mark unresolved or version-sensitive target behavior as TBD.
When admitting source basis, record the source-basis admission owner and ruling record as TBD unless a later sealed brief assigns that responsibility.
To draft the target profile contract, reference DEL-17-02 package/profile/stable-ID/manifest/loss-report concepts.
When drafting the target profile contract, declare target version basis or TBD.
When drafting the target profile contract, declare unit policy, coordinate policy, source-basis IDs, stable-ID behavior, loss-report policy, and external execution policy where applicable.
When drafting the target profile contract, classify each entity or behavior family as exported, omitted, approximated, delegated, unsupported, or TBD.
When drafting the target profile contract, preserve sidecar mapping requirements where target artifacts cannot carry canonical IDs.

When reviewing adapter boundary obligations, confirm adapter operations cannot bypass schema validation, unit checks, provenance checks, diagnostics/result envelopes, protected-content screening, private-data controls, report controls, solver boundaries, rule-pack sandboxing, or professional-boundary wording.

When reviewing adapter boundary obligations, confirm any filesystem, network, process, storage, private-data, or rule-pack access remains denied unless a later approved runtime/sandbox design grants a bounded capability.
When reviewing adapter boundary obligations, confirm target options are treated as pass-through configuration and not as OpenPipeStress code-checking logic.

Validation checklist topic 'Source-basis completeness' expects a source-basis record or dossier entry with source location, source-basis ID, license/redistribution posture, admitted use, and review disposition.
Validation checklist topic 'Target version basis' expects a target profile record naming the target version basis or marking it TBD.
Validation checklist topic 'Units and coordinate conventions' expects a profile field, validation record, or review note confirming unit and coordinate policy, with unresolved cases remaining TBD.
Validation checklist topic 'Stable ID mapping and sidecars' expects an ID-map artifact, sidecar reference, or manifest entry, with omitted mappings requiring reasons.
Validation checklist topic 'Export package member inventory' expects a manifest or package-member list with emitted files, diagnostics, reports, hashes where applicable, and declared omissions.
Validation checklist topic 'Manifest and hash policy' expects a manifest record identifying deterministic text/JSON hashes or explaining why a hash is unavailable.

Validation checklist topic 'Loss-report categories' expects a loss report with affected canonical IDs, category, severity, target artifact if any, reason, source-basis reference, and downstream implication.
Validation checklist topic 'Diagnostics and severity routing' expects a validation report or diagnostics envelope preserving warnings, blockers, and target limitations.

Validation checklist topic 'Privacy and protected-content screening' expects a review note or contribution disposition showing public/private/protected-content status and quarantine/rejection when needed.

Validation checklist topic 'External execution ownership when applicable' expects a run manifest or review note showing user-owned executable/service, target version/profile version, preserved run artifact, and non-authoritative status.

Validation checklist topic 'No compatibility/code-compliance/release/formal-validation/professional-acceptance wording' expects a boundary review note confirming prohibited claims were not introduced.
Do not implement adapter code from this Phase A contract.
Dispatch future implementation only under a sealed deliverable with explicit write scope.
Keep each target-specific writer, parser, harness, fixture, or schema change inside its approved deliverable scope.
Preserve all unresolved target behavior as TBD until the later deliverable has source and validation evidence.

Candidate future work 'Concrete schema layout' has candidate owner DEL-17 target implementation deliverables or DEL-10 adapter framework work, gated on JSON Schema 2020-12 and package/profile contract alignment.

Candidate future work 'Runtime/API surface and permission taxonomy' has candidate owner DEL-10-01 public API/plugin boundary and DEL-10-02 import/export adapter framework, gated until runtime grants, sandbox capability approval, filesystem/network/process access, and package layout are named by later authority.

Candidate future work 'Sample adapter and adapter test harness' has candidate owner a later adapter SDK implementation tranche under PKG-17 or PKG-10, gated on invented or rights-cleared fixtures only with no implementation from this Phase A contract.

Candidate future work 'Target-specific source dossiers' has candidate owner the DEL-17-01 source-basis workflow or a later target-specific source-intake deliverable, gated on admitted rights-cleared source basis.

Candidate future work 'Target-specific fixtures and validation tests' has candidate owner later target implementation deliverables such as native JSON, CAEPIPE MBF, PCF, or GLB/glTF adapters, gated on recorded fixture rights, target version basis, loss-report obligations, and validation evidence path.
DEL-17-09 verification includes a four-document structure check for Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.

DEL-17-09 verification includes manual source-grounding review against local _CONTEXT.md, _REFERENCES.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, DEL-17-01, DEL-17-02, project governance docs, and the export interoperability plan.
DEL-17-09 verification includes a write-scope review confirming only authorized DEL-17-09 files were edited.

DEL-17-09 verification includes a boundary review confirming no implementation code, schemas, public API promise, compatibility claim, target support claim, protected standards data, proprietary examples, release claim, code-compliance claim, formal-validation claim, or professional claim was introduced.
The acceptance signoff record for DEL-17-09 reviews remains TBD: reviewer role, signoff format, and required approval artifact are not named by the available sources.
This Phase A run should leave Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, Procedure.md, a _STATUS.md update from OPEN to INITIALIZED when applicable, and _run_records/TASK_RUN_*.md.

Future target-admission runs should add records only under their own sealed write scope, with expected decision artifacts (target registry record, source-basis admission record, validation checklist record, run record) remaining TBD unless a later brief names them; MEMORY.md is intentionally not updated in this phase.

DEL-17-09 defines a contract-level export adapter SDK and target-admission model for future community or additional export targets, covering adapter obligations, target registry admission states, source-basis requirements, boundary contracts, and validation checklist expectations.

DEL-17-09 shall not implement source code, schemas, runtime loaders, public endpoints, package manifests, sample adapters, tests, external parser behavior, executable harnesses, or target-specific writers, and shall not make compatibility, target support, release, formal validation, code-compliance, or professional-acceptance claims.

DEL-17-09-REQ-001: the adapter SDK contract shall consume DEL-17-02 as its common export package/profile/stable-ID/manifest/loss-report contract and shall not redefine those package objects in incompatible terms.
DEL-17-09-REQ-002: additional targets shall provide their own admitted source basis before any target-specific behavior is described as supported, compatible, validated, or ready for use.

DEL-17-09-REQ-003: unknown, unsupported, version-sensitive, or source-insufficient target behavior shall remain TBD, unsupported, omitted, approximated, or delegated rather than becoming a support claim.

DEL-17-09-REQ-004: adapter participation shall require target version basis, unit policy, coordinate policy, stable-ID policy, source-basis IDs, loss-report policy, diagnostics policy, and boundary notes at the contract level; exact field names/layout remain TBD until later schema work.
DEL-17-09-REQ-005: adapter targets shall preserve canonical identity directly or through sidecar mapping when target artifacts cannot carry OpenPipeStress IDs.
DEL-17-09-REQ-006: every target adapter shall require a loss report, including for successful exports, so exported, omitted, approximated, delegated, unsupported, and TBD behavior remains visible.

DEL-17-09-REQ-007: adapter validation shall distinguish syntactic readiness, schema validation, unit and dimensional validation, provenance completeness, redistribution review, privacy classification, protected-content screening, mechanics readiness, rule-check readiness, export review, and human review.

DEL-17-09-REQ-008: adapter and target registry records shall not grant filesystem, network, process, private-data, report-control, solver, rule-pack, or storage access by default; runtime grant mechanics remain TBD.

DEL-17-09-REQ-009: public adapter templates and target examples shall use invented or otherwise rights-cleared data only, and shall not include protected standards data, proprietary commercial examples, copied vendor files, or private project data.

DEL-17-09-REQ-010: external execution, if a later target adapter needs it, shall be optional, user-owned, license-bound, and recorded as non-authoritative external-run evidence rather than professional acceptance.

DEL-17-09-REQ-011: adapter outputs, manifests, diagnostics, documentation, and checklist language shall not claim certification, sealing, approval, authentication, endorsement, code compliance, professional acceptance, formal solver validation, release readiness, or vendor compatibility.
DEL-17-09-REQ-012: future implementation work shall be bounded to later sealed deliverables and shall not be implied by this Phase A contract kit.

DEL-17-09-REQ-013: adapter contracts shall carry DEL-17-01 and DEL-17-02 source-basis refs, and any source_basis_admitted target shall carry target-specific source evidence beyond package-level contract refs.

Runtime permission taxonomy, sandbox capability approval, and grant-record ownership are not named by the available Phase A sources; they remain TBD and shall not be inferred from adapter manifest requests, target registry records, or candidate target names.

No protected engineering standard, vendor format standard, proprietary example, material allowable table, SIF/flexibility table, protected dimensional table, code-specific acceptance criterion, or private owner/project data is incorporated into DEL-17-09.

Applicable internal baselines include docs/CONTRACT.md, especially OPS-K-IP-1 through OPS-K-IP-3, OPS-K-DATA-1 through OPS-K-DATA-3, OPS-K-AUTH-1, OPS-K-UNIT-1, OPS-K-REPORT-1 through OPS-K-REPORT-2, OPS-K-PRIV-1 through OPS-K-PRIV-2, and OPS-K-AGENT-1 through OPS-K-AGENT-4.
docs/IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md is an applicable baseline for public/private data, provenance, quarantine, contribution review, and non-professional boundary policy.
docs/SPEC.md section 4.5 is an applicable baseline for plugin and adapter no-bypass controls.
DEL-17-01 is an applicable baseline for admitted target source evidence and unresolved CAEPIPE/PCF/glTF target TBDs.
DEL-17-02 is an applicable baseline for export package, export profile, stable ID map, manifest, and loss-report contract objects.
Concrete additional target standards, formats, vendor APIs, target versions, and source-citation requirements are TBD until a later source-basis intake admits them.
DEL-17-09 makes no statement that any additional target is supported.
Verification of REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005, and REQ-006 is by contract review confirming alignment with DEL-17-02 package/profile/stable-ID/manifest/loss-report semantics.
Verification of REQ-002, REQ-004, and REQ-009 is by source-basis review confirming target-specific statements are source-grounded, explicitly TBD, or excluded.
Verification of REQ-007 and REQ-008 is by architecture/security review confirming adapter admission does not grant runtime permissions, storage access, external execution, or bypass privileges.
Verification of REQ-010 and REQ-011 is by professional/IP boundary review confirming no external-run, compatibility, validation, release, code-compliance, or professional-acceptance claim is present.
Verification of REQ-012 is by sealed-scope review confirming no implementation files, schemas, tests, package manifests, public API endpoints, or sibling deliverable files were modified.
Validation category 'Syntactic readiness and schema validation' is recorded TBD until concrete schema layout exists; later records should cite schema validation evidence when available.
Validation category 'Unit and dimensional validation' is recorded pass/fail/TBD against declared unit and coordinate policies; no silent unit default is acceptable.
Validation category 'Provenance completeness' records source-basis IDs, source location, license or redistribution posture, and review disposition, or is marked TBD/rejected.

Validation category 'Redistribution review, privacy classification, and protected-content screening' records public/private/protected-content disposition before public artifact use; suspected protected content is rejected or quarantined, not normalized into an example.

Validation category 'Mechanics readiness, rule-check readiness, and export review' records only evidence-supported readiness and does not convert target parser success into code-compliance, professional-acceptance, or solver-validation claims.
Validation category 'Human review' records reviewer role and signoff format as TBD unless a later sealed workflow names them.
